clue.text: Exotic dish found in eastern county where bodies were buried

indicators.note: the dish is found inside the county, so one set of letters sits within the other

parts.note: CAMBS is the short form of Cambridgeshire, a county in eastern England
a taco is a Mexican dish, exotic to a British diner

explanation.surface: A foreign meal turns up in East Anglia, at a spot where the dead were laid to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMBS is the usual abbreviation for Cambridgeshire, an English county in the east; TACO goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground cemeteries with burial recesses, as in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Conspirator about to start swindle — millions stolen

indicators.note: placed at the start, so this piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the millions are stolen away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a scam is a swindle

explanation.surface: A plotter is on the verge of launching a fraud in which millions go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Casca is one of the conspirators who stab Caesar in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca was one of the Roman plotters against Julius Caesar, and stabs him first in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Lever, prime requirement for the ship

indicators.note: the prime, or first, letter is what is required from the following word

parts.note: first letter of the
a rigger is a ship described by its rig, as in square-rigger

explanation.surface: Something essential for getting a vessel under way is a lever.
explanation.walkthrough: A rigger is a ship of a named rig, as in a square-rigger; T, the first letter of 'the', goes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trigger is a small lever pulled to fire a gun or set off a mechanism.

clue.text: Vehicle outside gala, one with ace facility for refreshments

indicators.note: the vehicle goes outside the gala, wrapping around it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a fete is a gala or open-air festivity
I is the Roman numeral for one
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: At a fair, a van parked by the festivities serves food and drink, with one stall rated top-notch.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, a place where refreshments are served.

clue.text: Do Old Trafford players emerge from this ancient industrial unit?

parts.note: Old Trafford is the home ground of Manchester United, known as Man U
a factory is where products come out from

explanation.surface: A joking question about whether Manchester United's footballers come out of some old works.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is the stadium of Manchester United football club, nicknamed Man U; the answer splits as MAN U FACTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufactory is an archaic word for a factory, a building where goods are made.

clue.text: Replace one sort of vessel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stand in for someone, as a substitute does
second meaning: short for submarine, a type of ship

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is to sub for someone; the noun is short for submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word is both a verb for substituting and a clipped form of submarine, a craft that dives.

clue.text: What's used in ceremonial — a thick stick

indicators.note: the letters needed are those used inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A description of a heavy rod carried at a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sits across the end of 'ceremonial', the 'a' and the start of 'thick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick bound with iron, carried by police in India.

clue.text: Short track leading to excellent porch

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
the track is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a lane is a narrow track
A1 means excellent, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A brief path runs up to a splendid veranda.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is often written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanai is a Hawaiian word for a veranda or roofed porch.

clue.text: Unimportant test with India against joining in

indicators.note: the two letters join the test by going into it

parts.note: a trial is a test
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A cricket Test against India is dismissed as unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little significance or value, so it means unimportant.

clue.text: Learning English to start with — tricky usually

indicators.note: tricky suggests something twisted or awkward, so the letters are rearranged
only the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of English

explanation.surface: Studying English as a beginner is generally hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: In general is an idiom meaning as a rule or for the most part.

clue.text: Nervy movements going round bog? Toughen up!

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: fits are sudden spasms or nervous movements
a fen is a marsh or bog

explanation.surface: Someone nervously twitching near a marsh is told to toughen up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen is to make or become firmer or more resolute, an idiomatic match for toughen up.

clue.text: Turning in close to meet bishop at entrance

indicators.note: the bishop stands at the entrance, so comes first

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the close of something is its ending

explanation.surface: Near the end of the service, someone turns to greet the bishop at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending means curving or veering, the same as turning.

clue.text: A king acquired the language of a particular class

definitions.text: the language of a particular class

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
got means acquired

explanation.surface: A monarch picks up the speech of a certain social group.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or slang peculiar to a group, such as thieves.

clue.text: Rosy-cheeked Scot or American?

parts.note: florid means ruddy or flushed in complexion
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scot's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a red-faced man hails from Scotland or the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'American' is defined by one example, someone from a single state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Floridian is a native of Florida, so one particular kind of American.

clue.text: Act as glutton, devouring ends of lettuce messily

indicators.note: done messily, the letters are thrown into disorder
the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: first and last letters of lettuce

explanation.surface: A greedy eater wolfs down the outer leaves of a lettuce untidily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devouring' looks like the glutton's action, but its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To overindulge is to eat or drink to excess, which is how a glutton behaves.

clue.text: Short priest, one despised

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the French word for a parish priest, taken here without its accent

explanation.surface: A small clergyman is held in contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel dog, and figuratively a contemptible person.

clue.text: Electrical device seen as top performer needing minimal current input

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: the current is put into the performer

parts.note: an actor is a performer
I is the physics symbol for current, a single letter

explanation.surface: A leading actor gets by on hardly any power from the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A capacitor is a component that stores electric charge in a circuit.

clue.text: Philanthropist given brief reprimand — declined to meet the Queen

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a rocket is a severe telling-off in British slang
fell means declined or dropped
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A benefactor, scolded briefly, then lost status before meeting the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone a rocket is British slang for a sharp reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: John D. Rockefeller gave away vast sums, making his name a byword for charitable wealth.

clue.text: Leaders of empire not trumpeted when we are living as followers?

definitions.note: a singular collective noun for a group of followers

indicators.note: the leading letters of each word are taken

parts.note: our age is the era in which we live

explanation.surface: Imperial rulers who keep quiet in modern times have hangers-on.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants and hangers-on accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Love and thanks received by fantastic sporting champion

indicators.note: the first pieces are taken in by the anagram, going inside it
fantastic suggests something fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is love, zero in tennis
TA is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A sports star accepts affection and gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting champion' reads as one phrase, but 'sporting' is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist is a leading advocate or supporter of a cause, a champion of it.

clue.text: Scientific unit needing old trees destroyed (fifty to go)

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are broken up and rearranged
the fifty must go, leaving the rest of the letters

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A unit of measurement requires the felling of ancient trees, fifty of them spared.
explanation.definitionFit: The oersted is the CGS unit of magnetic field strength, named after the Danish physicist.

clue.text: Length — short one extending end of railway

indicators.note: the short railway is extended by the next piece placed after it

parts.note: EL is the short name for an elevated railway, one of the kind in the clue

indicators.note: only the last letter is taken

parts.note: last letter of railway

explanation.surface: A brief stretch of track added on to a railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: An el is American shorthand for an elevated railway, so the 'short one' is a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The ell is an old English unit of measure for cloth, about 45 inches.

clue.text: Report of school in superior position being demolished?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school; up means in a higher or superior position

explanation.surface: A school report written while the place is being torn down.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known public school; ETON UP said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Food eaten up has been demolished, an informal sense of polishing off a meal.

clue.text: Abrupt son getting looked at gave gesture of respect

parts.note: curt means abrupt or brusque
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A brusque young man, being stared at, bowed in deference.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtsey is to bend the knees in a formal bow, traditionally performed by women.

clue.text: Drunk-sounding gentleman in Dorset for example

indicators.note: a drunk slurs words, so the gentleman's word is said aloud with a slur

parts.note: sire is a respectful word for a gentleman or lord

explanation.surface: A tipsy-sounding toff out in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Slurred as a drunk would say it, SIRE becomes SHIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county in south-west England, and shire is another word for county.

clue.text: Speak — do so quietly with face hidden

indicators.note: the face, the first letter, is concealed, so it goes

parts.note: to mutter is to speak quietly

explanation.surface: Telling someone to talk under their breath while covering their face.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say or speak aloud.

clue.text: Game to get embarrassed about, with more offensive language?

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed

explanation.surface: A rugby match turns into an embarrassing slanging match.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruder is the comparative of rude; foul-mouthed speech is ruder.

clue.text: Old levy — object when it is limited

indicators.note: it is limited, held in by the object around it

parts.note: a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Someone objects to an ancient tax being capped.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithing is the paying of tithes, a tenth of produce owed to the church.

clue.text: Rock with primate half visible?

indicators.note: only half the letters can be seen, the rest gone

parts.note: a gibbon is an ape, a primate

explanation.surface: Seeing only part of an ape on a famous rock, as with Gibraltar's apes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rock is a nickname for Gibraltar, shortened to Gib; its Barbary apes are famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Gib is the informal name for Gibraltar, known as the Rock.

clue.text: King Edmund like King Alfred?

parts.note: Lear is the king in Shakespeare's play
Ned is a short form of Edmund

explanation.surface: Comparing one Anglo-Saxon King Edmund to another, King Alfred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edmund' looks like one monarch but splits in two; neatly, Edmund is the villain of Shakespeare's King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was noted for scholarship and translating books, so he was erudite.

clue.text: Acceleration going down in journey to bring top place?

indicators.note: the acceleration goes down into the journey, inside it

parts.note: a ride is a journey
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Speeding downhill during a trip to reach the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the crest of a hill or roof, a high point.

clue.text: One who needs insects to thrive — such as hartebeest?

definitions.text: One who needs insects to thrive

parts.note: the antelope's name holds a buzzing insect within it, so it literally keeps one

explanation.surface: Asking whether an African antelope depends on insects to flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: HARTEBEEST has BEE inside it, so whimsically it is keeping a bee.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiarist relies on healthy colonies of bees for honey and a living.
